title: Normalized tensor comparison for a right exact strong monoidal functor
statement: Let C,D be braided closed monoidal Grothendieck abelian categories with additive tensor and functorial flat resolutions. Let E:C→D be additive, strong monoidal, left adjoint, preserving flat objects and quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes. Let LE:D(C)→D(D) be its total left derived functor. Given G≅LE, transport the left-derived cochain counit dP along this isomorphism to rP. There exists a unique family μ(K,L):GK tensor GL≅G(K tensor L), natural in each variable, for which G(μ_Q(P,Q)) followed by r(P tensor Q) and Q of the ordinary oplax tensorator equals μ(QP,QQ) inverse followed by rP tensor rQ and the target μ_Q, whenever P,Q are flat-term K-flat cochain complexes. Here μ_Q is the fixed localization tensorator; no exactness of E is assumed.

source.place: Tags 06YY and 07A4; formal two-variable derived universal property and flat models

proof.text: Choose the class of homotopy complexes that are both K-flat and whose E-image is K-flat. A functorial flat resolution is in this class because E preserves flat objects and is a left adjoint, hence preserves the colimits in its construction. These models give a left derivability structure.

Derive the two bifunctors E(P tensor Q) and EP tensor EQ on pairs of these models. Their counits are respectively LE of the source localization tensorator followed by the E counit, and the two E counits followed by the target tensorator. K-flatness makes both invertible there. Derive the ordinary oplax tensorator using leftDerived₂NatTrans. Since E is strong monoidal its derived comparison is an isomorphism, with the required homotopy counit equation.

Express the cochain localization tensorator as the homotopy tensorator conjugated by qP,qQ,q(P tensor Q). Naturality of q for the ordinary oplax tensorator and naturality of the derived comparison convert the homotopy equation into the cochain equation. Conjugate the comparison along G≅LE to obtain μ.

Every derived object has a flat-term K-flat representative with K-flat E-image by the same flat resolution. On two such representatives rP,rQ and the target tensorator are invertible, so the counit equation determines μ inverse by cancellation. Naturality transports the equality along isomorphisms from these representatives to arbitrary objects, proving uniqueness.

theorem rightExact_tensorComparison_existsUnique
    (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] [F.PreservesKFlatQuasiIso]
    [F.PreservesFlat] [F.IsLeftAdjoint] [F.Monoidal]
    (G : DerivedCategory C ⥤ DerivedCategory D) (e : G ≅ F.leftDerivedFunctor)
    (r : ∀ P : CochainComplex C ℤ,
      G.obj ((DerivedCategory.Q (C := C)).obj P) ⟶
        (DerivedCategory.Q (C := D)).obj ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P))
    (hr : ∀ P, r P = e.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) ≫ F.rightExact_cochainCounit P) :
    ∃! μ : ∀ K L : DerivedCategory C,
      ((curriedTensor (DerivedCategory D)).obj (G.obj K)).obj (G.obj L) ≅
        G.obj (((curriedTensor (DerivedCategory C)).obj K).obj L),
      (∀ {K K'} (f : K ⟶ K') L,
        ((curriedTensor (DerivedCategory D)).map (G.map f)).app (G.obj L) ≫ (μ K' L).hom =
          (μ K L).hom ≫ G.map (((curriedTensor (DerivedCategory C)).map f).app L)) ∧
      (∀ K {L L'} (f : L ⟶ L'),
        ((curriedTensor (DerivedCategory D)).obj (G.obj K)).map (G.map f) ≫ (μ K L').hom =
          (μ K L).hom ≫ G.map (((curriedTensor (DerivedCategory C)).obj K).map f)) ∧
      rightExactTensorModelNormalization F G r μ
